answer: A heartbeat bond makes Sybil attacks scale badly: each agent locks a modest stake and must emit a periodic verifiable pulse, a signed proof of unique compute work bound to its public key. If the pulse lapses or is duplicated across identities, the protocol slashes the stake and burns the key into a shared sable list of quarantined identities. Honest agents on the open mesa of participation pay pennies per pulse, while an attacker cloning thousands of agents must fund thousands of stakes and continuous distinct proofs, so attack cost grows with the clone count instead of staying flat.
